own:
Nudges are optional. They are a tool that we've built into the trading system as an optional tool to get the other party's attention, and it can be used at a maximum of every 15 minutes. There has to be 15 minutes in between using it because it is rather annoying.

If the buyer who put up the Monero and has fully escrowed it decides to cancel, it does not give a warning to the other party and give them a chance. The person decided to cancel, and the refund process of the Monero begins. The trade is complete once all 10 confirmations have completed.

It is up to that buyer whether they want to use the nudge feature or not. Obviously, we are going to inform them about it when the trade window that lists all the things that are specific to the seller or the buyer, that list of items, it'll be one of those things that is going to tell them about the nudge feature and encourage them to use it if they do have an unresponsive partner. It saves them for having to restart a new trade with somebody else.

Having a weak or strong login has nothing to do with canceling.

I'm afraid if the seller decides to wait until the entire 90 minutes are up and then decides to send the money to the person, they almost deserve to experience having that person cancel it on them even though they've sent them the money, and then they'll have to dispute it to get their money back. It's pretty stupid to wait the entire period of time that you've been allotted to send the money to someone and choose to send it after that time period is up.
question: When the seller asks for the escrow back because the buyer hasn't paid, the buyer gets a 15-minute warning. Should opening that warning count only from a strong login?
